items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Sometimes it was a Dixieland band and Godfrey would play along with his ukulele

ctx.x: Some of our younger viewers might not remember the Arthur Godfrey Show, but did you have some experiences in there that were new? It must have been that every week something would come along.

It was a daily show and additional — a daily radio show — and additional occasional television shows. Well I really was in a position to be forced to learn very quickly quite a number of things. I had to make sure my conducting was up to standards, because many of those things were not just beating off tempo, they were conducting music comedy or even light opera kind of material. And it was a peculiar band. I acquired the band you might say, and it already included Lee Irwin on organ, and Lud Flato on piano. So…
Were you responsible for sound effects, anything like that?
